correctness.rationale: The alignment lemma reduces nonoccurrence in the factor language to all k residues being obstructed by missing-block occurrences, including arbitrary partial endpoint blocks. Any k occurrences in different residues form a weighted residue spanning path. Kruskal costs each proper period p_i exactly (g_(i-1)-g_i)*p_i, plus (g_m-1)*(k+1), where g_i are successive gcd values. A translated-coset Hamilton path achieves exactly these positive forward gaps, and overlapping copies are consistent because sums of proper periods shorter than k remain periods. This proves the infinite-domain equality; independent KMP and direct NFA BFS agree on 508 and 124 binary instances, respectively. All k>=2 and all finite alphabets of size>=2 are quantified, including constants and unbordered words.

value.rationale: The one-hole full uniform code is a canonical extremal completeness object. Determining the exact shortest absent factor for every missing word, including those with multiple interacting periods, strengthens prior unbordered-only exact classification. The formula is structural and infinite: successive gcd reductions quantify how cheaper period edges eliminate expensive code-boundary transitions. It gives a constructive witness and arithmetic computation without exponentially enumerating the code. It does not imply a theorem for arbitrary incomplete codes.
